title: Homily XXIV
subtitle: Matthew 7:21
author: chrysostom
excerpt: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of Heaven, but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in…

footnotes.1: [ἀγαπητν; probably the sense is rather: “it must suffice them,” etc.—R.]
footnotes.2: Rom. ii. 17, 18. [R.V., “But if thou bearest the name of a Jew,” etc., following the reading ε δ, which is abundantly attested. Chrysostom has ἴδεἀγπη.—R.]
footnotes.3: Mark ix. 38; Luke ix. 49. [“Demons,” so in the New Testament passages.—R.]
footnotes.7: Matt. vii. 24. [R.V., “Every one, therefore which beareth these words of mine, and doeth them, shall be likened.” The Greek text in the Homily is identical with that accepted in the R.V.—R.]
footnotes.8: [ερπ, a strait, where the ebb and flow is great and frequent. See Liddell and Scott, Greek Lexicon.—R.]
footnotes.10: τν κοινν δικν πραγματεεσθα σε παρασκευζωνπραγματεεσθαι. [The verb means “to engage in business,” and it is an easy transition to the successful result of trading. The Latin rendering of Montfaucon is: ac tibi providens, ut a communi illa reddenda ratione te expedias —R.]
footnotes.18: Matt. xiv. 2; Luke ix. 9. [The verb ἀνελον, which occurs here, is not found in the New Testament accounts of Herod’s language.—R.]
